sub-literals.rs.reason: batch-2 literal-sub-two-impls: 3 - 1 with Sub for usize and u8; builtin integral rule unifies literal operands with the usize result

mul-const-argument.rs.reason: portable-simd to_bytes shape: { 2 * 4 } usize const argument with Mul for usize and u8

sub-impl-lengths.rs.reason: array_impl_default shape: [T; 2], [T; (2 - 1)], [T; ((2 - 1) - 1)] with Sub for usize and u8 are distinct impls

shift-result-lhs.rs.reason: const u8 = 1 << 3: shift result is the lhs type; the only u8 impl Shl<u32> fixes the rhs

shift-rhs-not-unified.rs.reason: const u32 = 1 << 3 with Shl<u32> and Shl<u8> for u32: shift never unifies rhs with lhs, rhs stays ambiguous, falls back to i32 and u32: Shl<i32> is missing (E0277)

float-literals.rs.reason: f32 return 1.0 + 2.0 with Add for f32 and f64: builtin float rule unifies operands with the result

reference-rhs.rs.reason: 1 + x with x: &u8; builtin rule peels one reference and unifies the literal with u8; Add<&u8> for u8 is selected over Add<&u8> for u16

user-impl-by-trait.rs.reason: 3 * m with m: M is not builtin; trait selection picks the only Mul<M> impl (u8) with Output M

mixed-width.rs.reason: u8 - usize: both integral so the builtin rule demands equal operand types even though Sub<usize> for u8 exists (E0308)

assign-literal.rs.reason: x += 2 with x: u8 and AddAssign for u8 and AddAssign<u16> for u8: builtin rule unifies the literal with u8

compare-literal.rs.reason: n == 3 with n: u8, PartialEq for u8 and PartialEq<u16> for u8: builtin comparison unifies the literal with u8

compare-mixed-width.rs.reason: u8 == u16: both scalar so the builtin comparison demands equal operand types (E0308) despite PartialEq<u16> for u8
